title: Building an AI-powered app
summary: Architecture, keys, cost and trust, the parts that matter in production.

cards.title: The basic shape
cards.body:
**Your app → your server → the model provider's API → your server → your app.**

- Never put an API key inside an APK. Apps can be unpacked and the key extracted. Keep keys on a server you control, or let users paste their own key and store it encrypted (Android Keystore).
- Your server can add rate limits, logging, caching and abuse protection.

cards.title: What changes compared to normal code
cards.body:
- **Cost and latency per call**: every request is billed by the amount of text in and out, and takes noticeable time. Stream long answers so users see progress.
- **Non-determinism**: the same input can give different outputs. Test with many examples, not one.
- **Trust**: ground answers in your own data (retrieval), ask for structured output (JSON) you can validate, and show users when content is AI-generated.

cards.title: A LogicForge-shaped example
cards.body: An "explain this code" button could send a snippet to a model and show the answer. A safer design asks the model to answer in the app's diagram language (the English → Diagram sandbox), so the output is constrained and checkable before it's shown. That's the plan in ADR-0004.

cards.question: Where should the API key for a paid AI service live?
choices: On a server you control (or entered by the user and stored encrypted)
cards.explain: Anything shipped in the APK can be extracted. Keys belong on a backend, or with the user who pays for them.

cards.question: Why ask a model for JSON instead of free text, when your app will act on the answer?
choices: You can validate it before using it
cards.explain: Structured output can be parsed and checked against a schema; free text can't be trusted to have the shape your code expects.
